;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
;; IMPL-013: zetl search — Tantivy Full-Text Search, Graph Scoping, and
;;           Browser Search
;; Implementation plan for SPEC-013
;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(meta plan
  (id "IMPL-013")
  (title "zetl search — Tantivy Full-Text Search, Graph Scoping, and Browser Search")
  (version "0.1.0")
  (status "active")
  (created "2026-03-01")
  (author "agent:claude")
  (spec "SPEC-013")
  (description "Replace grep-based search with Tantivy inverted index. Phase 1: add tantivy, build search index during `zetl index`, refactor `zetl search` to query Tantivy with BM25 scoring, add heading-aware context, support lazy index construction. Phase 2: add --near/--depth graph-scoped search via bidirectional BFS. Phase 3: expose /api/search in serve mode and upgrade Cmd+K to full-text search. Phase 4: emit search-index.json during build and embed client-side JS BM25 scorer. Covers REQ-013-001 through REQ-013-015, ADR-013-001 through ADR-013-004."))

;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
;; Agents
;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(given agent-claude-available)

;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
;; Phase 1 — Tantivy Index & Core Search
;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
;;
;; Goal: Replace grep-based search entirely with Tantivy. zetl index builds
;; a search index alongside the link graph. zetl search queries Tantivy for
;; BM25-scored results with line-level positions and heading context. Lazy
;; index construction when no index exists. All existing search tests must
;; be updated to the new output schema. This is the largest phase — it
;; touches Cargo.toml, search.rs, main.rs (cmd_index, cmd_search), cli.rs,
;; and introduces a new search_index module.
;; ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

;; ── Task: Add tantivy dependency ──────────────────────────────────────────

(given task-add-tantivy)
(given no-deps-add-tantivy)

(meta task-add-tantivy
  (description "Add tantivy crate to Cargo.toml. Use the latest stable version (0.22+). No feature flags needed beyond defaults. Run cargo check to verify the dependency resolves and compiles cleanly. Tantivy pulls in ~50 transitive dependencies and adds ~5-8 MB to binary size (acceptable per ADR-013-001, SPEC-013 §9.4). Do NOT add any other new dependencies in this task.")
  (acceptance "cargo check passes with tantivy importable; no other code changes; dependency resolves without conflicts with existing deps (petgraph, serde, tokio)"))

(normally r-ready-add-tantivy
  (and task-add-tantivy no-deps-add-tantivy)
  ready-add-tantivy)

(normally r-assign-add-tantivy
  (and ready-add-tantivy agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-add-tantivy-claude)

;; ── Task: Create search index module ──────────────────────────────────────

(given task-search-index-module)

(meta task-search-index-module
  (description "Create src/search_index.rs with the Tantivy index management layer. This module encapsulates all Tantivy interaction:

Schema: Three fields per document:
  - page_name: STRING (stored, indexed for filtering)
  - path: STRING (stored, not indexed)
  - body: TEXT (indexed for full-text search, stored)

Tokenization: Tantivy's default tokenizer (lowercase, split on whitespace/punctuation).

Index location: .zetl/search/ directory.

Public API:
  - SearchIndex::build(vault_root, files: &[ParsedFile]) -> Result<SearchIndex>
    Creates/opens .zetl/search/, iterates files, extracts body text using scanner::body_text_ranges(), creates one Tantivy document per file. Clears and rebuilds the full index (incremental update handled at the caller level via cache).
  - SearchIndex::open(vault_root) -> Result<Option<SearchIndex>>
    Opens an existing index from .zetl/search/. Returns None if directory doesn't exist.
  - SearchIndex::query(query_str, limit) -> Result<Vec<SearchHit>>
    Parses query with QueryParser against the body field, executes with TopDocs collector, returns Vec of (page_name, path, score) tuples.
  - SearchIndex::reader() -> Result<IndexReader>
    For serve mode: returns a reader that can be held across requests.

SearchHit struct: { page_name: String, path: String, score: f64 }

Body text extraction: For each file, concatenate the byte ranges from body_text_ranges() into a single string. This reuses the same exclusion logic as SPEC-002 (no frontmatter, code blocks, inline code, HTML comments). Import body_text_ranges from scanner.rs.

Error handling: Return anyhow::Result with context about which file or query failed.

REQ-013-001, ADR-013-001.")
  (acceptance "SearchIndex compiles; build() creates .zetl/search/ with valid Tantivy index; open() reads existing index; query() returns BM25-scored results; body text excludes frontmatter/code/comments; cargo check passes"))

(normally r-ready-search-index-module
  (and task-search-index-module completed-add-tantivy)
  ready-search-index-module)

(normally r-assign-search-index-module
  (and ready-search-index-module agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-search-index-module-claude)

;; ── Task: Heading detection ───────────────────────────────────────────────

(given task-heading-detection)

(meta task-heading-detection
  (description "Add heading detection to src/search.rs (or a dedicated module). Implement per SPEC-013 §4.6:

Public API:
  - detect_headings(content: &str, body_text_ranges: &[(usize, usize)]) -> Vec<FileHeading>
    Scan line by line. For lines matching ^#{1,6}\\s, check if the byte offset falls within a body_text_range. If so, record FileHeading { byte_offset, level, text }. Text is the heading stripped of leading # chars and trailing whitespace.
  - find_heading_for_offset(headings: &[FileHeading], byte_offset: usize) -> (Option<String>, Option<u8>)
    Binary search for the largest heading byte_offset <= the match byte_offset. Returns (heading_text, heading_level) or (None, None) if no preceding heading.

FileHeading struct: { byte_offset: usize, level: u8, text: String }

Headings inside code blocks, frontmatter, or HTML comments are excluded by the body_text_ranges filter (ADR-013-003). Setext headings are not detected (out of scope).

REQ-013-010, REQ-013-011, ADR-013-003.")
  (acceptance "detect_headings finds ATX headings in body text only; headings in code blocks are excluded; find_heading_for_offset returns nearest preceding heading; returns None before first heading; cargo check passes"))

(normally r-ready-heading-detection
  (and task-heading-detection completed-add-tantivy)
  ready-heading-detection)

(normally r-assign-heading-detection
  (and ready-heading-detection agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-heading-detection-claude)

;; ── Task: Integrate search index into zetl index ──────────────────────────

(given task-integrate-index)

(meta task-integrate-index
  (description "Extend cmd_index() in src/main.rs to build the Tantivy search index after building the link graph. Call SearchIndex::build() with the parsed files. Only build/rebuild for files that need re-indexing (use the same mtime cache invalidation as the graph — files_needing_reparse() already identifies changed files). For --no-cache, rebuild the entire index from scratch (delete .zetl/search/ and rebuild).

Add new JSON output fields per CON-013-002:
  - search_index_docs: number of documents in the search index
  - search_index_size_kb: size of .zetl/search/ directory in KB

Add verbose stderr output per OBS-013-001:
  - Documents indexed, index size, index build time (ms)

Note on incremental indexing: For v1, the simplest approach is to delete and rebuild the full index when any file changes. Tantivy index merging is complex; since NFR-013-001 requires ≤5s for 10,000 files, a full rebuild is acceptable. The cache layer at the cmd_index level already knows which files changed — the index layer just builds from the full file set.

REQ-013-001, REQ-013-003, CON-013-002.")
  (acceptance "zetl index builds search index in .zetl/search/; JSON output includes search_index_docs and search_index_size_kb; --no-cache forces full rebuild; --verbose shows index stats; index content matches body text of all vault files"))

(normally r-ready-integrate-index
  (and task-integrate-index completed-search-index-module)
  ready-integrate-index)

(normally r-assign-integrate-index
  (and ready-integrate-index agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-integrate-index-claude)

;; ── Task: Refactor search to use Tantivy ──────────────────────────────────

(given task-refactor-search)

(meta task-refactor-search
  (description "Rewrite src/search.rs to query Tantivy instead of grep-scanning files. This is the core replacement per ADR-013-001.

Updated SearchMatch struct (SPEC-013 §4.7):
  pub struct SearchMatch {
      pub page: String,
      pub path: String,
      pub line: u32,
      pub column: u32,
      pub context: Option<String>,
      pub heading: Option<String>,      // NEW: enclosing heading text
      pub heading_level: Option<u8>,    // NEW: heading depth (1-6)
      pub score: f64,                   // NEW: BM25 score
  }

Updated SearchOutput struct:
  pub struct SearchOutput {
      pub query: String,
      pub total_matches: usize,
      pub results: Vec<SearchMatch>,
      // near/depth/neighbourhood_size added in Phase 2
  }

Remove: SearchConfig.regex field, SearchConfig.body_only field (always body-only now), build_matcher(), Matcher enum, the entire grep-based find_matches_in_content().

Query flow (SPEC-013 §4.4):
  1. Open or lazily build the Tantivy index.
  2. Parse query with QueryParser against body field.
  3. Execute with TopDocs collector, limited to --limit.
  4. For each matched document:
     a. Read the original file from disk.
     b. Compute body_text_ranges.
     c. Scan body text for query term occurrences (case-insensitive by default, case-sensitive with --case-sensitive). Find line/column for each occurrence.
     d. Detect headings via detect_headings().
     e. Attach heading context via find_heading_for_offset().
     f. Emit SearchMatch entries with the document's BM25 score.
  5. Order results by descending score, ties broken by path (ascending) then line (ascending).

The re-scanning step (4b-c) is necessary because Tantivy provides document-level scores but not character offsets. Split the query string on whitespace to get individual terms for re-scanning.

Retain: --case-sensitive flag (for re-scan), --path filter (applied to Tantivy results), --context chars, --limit.
Remove: --regex flag, --all flag.

REQ-013-002, REQ-013-005, CON-013-001.")
  (acceptance "zetl search returns BM25-scored results from Tantivy; every result has score, heading, heading_level fields; line/column positions are accurate; --case-sensitive works; --path filter works; --context works; --regex and --all removed from CLI; results ordered by score desc, then path asc, then line asc"))

(normally r-ready-refactor-search
  (and task-refactor-search completed-search-index-module completed-heading-detection)
  ready-refactor-search)

(normally r-assign-refactor-search
  (and ready-refactor-search agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-refactor-search-claude)

;; ── Task: Update CLI flags ────────────────────────────────────────────────

(given task-update-cli)

(meta task-update-cli
  (description "Update the Search subcommand in src/cli.rs:

Remove:
  - --regex flag
  - --all flag

Retain (unchanged):
  - <QUERY> positional argument
  - --case-sensitive flag
  - --path <GLOB> flag
  - --context <N> flag
  - --limit <N> flag (default 50)
  - -f <FORMAT> flag (json/table)

The --near and --depth flags are added in Phase 2.

Update cmd_search() in main.rs to match: remove regex/all handling, update SearchConfig construction, update JSON and table output to include score, heading, heading_level fields. Table format per CON-013-001: Page | Score | Line | Heading | Context.

REQ-013-002, CON-013-001.")
  (acceptance "CLI accepts all retained flags; --regex and --all are gone; JSON output includes score/heading/heading_level on every result; table output shows score and heading columns; cargo check passes"))

(normally r-ready-update-cli
  (and task-update-cli completed-refactor-search)
  ready-update-cli)

(normally r-assign-update-cli
  (and ready-update-cli agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-update-cli-claude)

;; ── Task: Lazy index construction ─────────────────────────────────────────

(given task-lazy-index)

(meta task-lazy-index
  (description "Implement lazy index construction in the search path per REQ-013-004. When zetl search is invoked and no .zetl/search/ directory exists (SearchIndex::open returns None):

  1. Print to stderr: 'Building search index (run `zetl index` to avoid this delay on future queries)'
  2. Scan the vault (reuse the pipeline's scan_vault + parse flow).
  3. Build the index via SearchIndex::build().
  4. Persist the index in .zetl/search/ for future queries.
  5. Continue with the search query.

This should be integrated into the search_vault() function or cmd_search() in main.rs. The lazy build does NOT build the link graph (only the search index). This means --near is unavailable without zetl index, but basic search works without prior indexing.

REQ-013-004.")
  (acceptance "zetl search works without prior zetl index; stderr shows building message; .zetl/search/ created and persisted; subsequent searches use the persisted index; search results are BM25-scored"))

(normally r-ready-lazy-index
  (and task-lazy-index completed-refactor-search)
  ready-lazy-index)

(normally r-assign-lazy-index
  (and ready-lazy-index agent-claude-available)
  assign-to-lazy-index-claude)

;; ── Task: Verify Phase 1 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

(given task-verify-phase1)

(meta task-verify-phase1
  (description "End-to-end verification of Phase 1. Test against the demo-vault or a purpose-built test vault:

  1. zetl index builds .zetl/search/ — JSON output includes search_index_docs and search_index_size_kb.
  2. zetl search 'term' returns BM25-scored results — every result has score, heading, heading_level fields.
  3. Relevance ranking: a page with many mentions of a term scores higher than one with a single mention (TEST-013-002).
  4. Exclusion zones: terms in frontmatter, code blocks, inline code, HTML comments are NOT found (TEST-013-001).
  5. Line-level results: multiple occurrences in the same file produce separate results with correct line/column, all sharing the same score (TEST-013-005).
  6. Heading context: matches under headings show correct heading/level; matches before first heading show null (TEST-013-010).
  7. Headings in code blocks are not used as enclosing headings (TEST-013-011).
  8. Index invalidation: modify a file, re-run zetl index, verify new content is searchable (TEST-013-003).
  9. --no-cache forces full rebuild (TEST-013-003).
  10. Lazy index: delete .zetl/search/, run zetl search — index built on the fly, stderr message shown (TEST-013-004).
  11. --case-sensitive flag works.
  12. --path filter works.
  13. --context flag works.
  14. --limit flag works.

(meta task-neighbourhood-bfs
  (description "Add a neighbourhood() method to LinkGraph in src/graph.rs. Algorithm per SPEC-013 §4.5:

  pub fn neighbourhood(&self, anchor: &str, depth: usize) -> Result<HashSet<String>>

  1. Resolve anchor to a node in the graph. Error if not found (with suggested similar names via the existing resolution logic).
  2. Initialize visited = {anchor}, queue = [(anchor, 0)].
  3. While queue not empty:
     a. Pop (page, d). If d >= depth, skip.
     b. For each neighbour (both outgoing AND incoming edges — bidirectional BFS):
        If not visited: add to visited, push (neighbour, d + 1).
  4. Return visited (the set of page names within depth hops).

Use petgraph's neighbors_directed(Outgoing) and neighbors_directed(Incoming) to get both edge directions.

The anchor page itself is always included in the result set.

NFR-013-004 target: ≤50ms for 10,000 pages at depth 3 with average degree 5.

REQ-013-006, ADR-013-002.")

  (spec "SPEC-006")
  (description "Implement a content-addressed Merkle tree built transparently during zetl index. Every block-level AST node is BLAKE3-hashed into a hierarchy. Four phases: P0 core Merkle infrastructure, P1 section grounding and drift, P2 explicit grounding and content discovery, P3 tests and observability."))

  (status "active")

;; Task metadata
(meta task-pure-core
  (description "Implement pure core functions: chunk_page, reciprocal_rank_fusion, cosine_similarity, detect_stale_chunks in src/semantic/core.rs")
  (acceptance "All pure functions are free of I/O; chunk_page splits at h2 boundaries; RRF produces correct ordering; cosine_similarity returns f32 in [0.0,1.0]; all unit tests pass")
  (context-files "src/semantic/core.rs")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic" "lint:cargo clippy --features semantic"))

(meta task-onnx-embedding-shell
  (description "Implement effectful embedding shell in src/semantic/mod.rs: embed_chunks via ort ONNX session, VectorIndex::build, VectorIndex::open, VectorIndex::query, VectorIndex::embed_query")
  (acceptance "VectorIndex::build creates vectors/ directory; open reads it back; round-trip produces identical results; embed_chunks returns 384-dim normalised vectors; TEST-118 and TEST-119 pass")
  (context-files "src/semantic/mod.rs" "Cargo.toml")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic" "lint:cargo clippy --features semantic"))

(meta task-vector-index-storage
  (description "Implement storage layout at .zetl/search/vectors/: index.bin (flat mmap-friendly vector file), chunks.json (chunk metadata with page, heading, content_hash), model.json (model name + dimension)")
  (acceptance "Storage layout matches spec; index.bin is mmap-readable; chunks.json round-trips correctly; model.json validates on open; REQ-093 satisfied")
  (context-files "src/semantic/mod.rs")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic"))

(meta task-chunking
  (description "Implement heading-level chunking strategy: split pages at ## boundaries, embed short pages (< 512 tokens) whole, each chunk carries page_name, path, heading, content_hash, embedding")
  (acceptance "chunk_page splits at h2 boundaries; join(chunks) == original body; pages under 512 tokens remain whole; TEST-120 passes with property-based tests; REQ-100 satisfied")
  (context-files "src/semantic/core.rs")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic"))

(meta task-incremental-rebuild
  (description "Implement incremental embedding rebuild in zetl index: BLAKE3-hash each chunk, compare against chunks.json, re-embed only stale chunks, write updated vectors and metadata")
  (acceptance "Changing one page re-embeds only that page's chunks; unchanged pages are skipped; TEST-123 passes; REQ-097 satisfied")
  (context-files "src/semantic/mod.rs" "src/cli.rs")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic"))

(meta task-semantic-cli
  (description "Implement zetl search --semantic <QUERY> CLI flag: embed query, run VectorIndex::query, return SearchOutput JSON ranked by cosine similarity with score in [0.0,1.0]; handle missing index and feature-not-compiled errors")
  (acceptance "Results ranked by cosine similarity; each result includes page, path, heading, score; --limit respected; missing index prints clear error; TEST-114 and TEST-115 pass; REQ-094, REQ-098, REQ-099 satisfied")
  (context-files "src/cli.rs" "src/main.rs")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic"))

  (description "Implement zetl search --hybrid <QUERY> CLI flag: run BM25 and vector search in parallel, fuse via RRF, apply --near graph scoping after fusion, return fused SearchOutput")
  (acceptance "Fused results combine BM25 and vector signals; --near intersects with graph neighbourhood; score is RRF fusion score; TEST-116 and TEST-117 pass; REQ-095, REQ-101 satisfied")
  (context-files "src/cli.rs" "src/main.rs")
  (evaluate-checks "test:cargo test --features semantic"))

;; Plan: Ratatui Terminal UI for zetl
(meta plan
  (id "IMPL-TUI")
  (title "Ratatui Terminal UI for zetl")
  (version "1.0.0")
  (status "active")
  (created "2026-02-19")
  (author "agent:claude")
  (description "Add an interactive terminal UI to zetl using ratatui, providing a dashboard with vault stats, page browser, link explorer, search, and diagnostics viewer"))

;; Agent
(given agent-claude-available)

;; ── Tasks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

;; Phase 1: Foundation
(given task-deps)
(given no-deps-deps)
(meta task-deps
  (description "Add ratatui, crossterm, and tui-input dependencies to Cargo.toml")
  (acceptance "cargo check passes with new deps; no version conflicts"))

(given task-app-scaffold)
(meta task-app-scaffold
  (description "Create src/tui/ module with App struct, event loop, and basic terminal setup/teardown using crossterm alternate screen and raw mode")
  (acceptance "zetl tui launches, shows blank screen, quits on 'q' key"))

;; Phase 2: Core Views
(given task-dashboard)
(meta task-dashboard
  (description "Build dashboard tab showing vault stats: page count, link count, dead links, orphans, connected components, and most-linked pages as a bar/list")
  (acceptance "Dashboard renders vault stats correctly; updates on tab switch"))

(given task-page-list)
(meta task-page-list
  (description "Build page list tab with scrollable list of all pages, filterable by typing; highlight selected page")
  (acceptance "All pages shown; typing filters list; arrow keys scroll; selection highlights"))

(given task-link-explorer)
(meta task-link-explorer
  (description "Build link explorer tab: select a page to see forward links and backlinks in side-by-side panes; navigate into linked pages")
  (acceptance "Forward and backlinks render for selected page; can navigate to linked pages"))

(given task-search-view)
(meta task-search-view
  (description "Build search tab with text input field and results list showing matches with context; navigate results")
  (acceptance "Typing queries produces results; results show page, line, and context; Enter opens link explorer for selected result"))

(given task-diagnostics)
(meta task-diagnostics
  (description "Build diagnostics tab showing dead links, orphans, and syntax errors in categorized lists")
  (acceptance "All diagnostics from check command shown; color-coded by severity"))

;; Phase 3: Polish
(given task-keybindings)
(meta task-keybindings
  (description "Add help overlay showing keybindings (? key); implement tab switching with number keys and Tab; consistent navigation across views")
  (acceptance "? shows help; 1-5 switch tabs; Tab cycles; Esc closes overlays; consistent vim-style j/k navigation"))

(given task-cli-integration)
(meta task-cli-integration
  (description "Add 'tui' subcommand to CLI via clap; wire it to launch the TUI app with vault scanning pipeline")
  (acceptance "zetl tui launches interactive UI; zetl tui -d <dir> works; existing commands unchanged"))

;; Fix plan for IMPL-020 second code review
(meta plan
  (id "FIX-020-review-2")
  (title "Fix IMPL-020 Second Code Review Issues")
  (version "1.0.0")
  (status "active")
  (created "2026-03-26")
  (author "agent:claude")
  (description "Address critical, important, and suggested fixes from second comprehensive code review"))

;; Single agent
(given agent-claude-available)

;; ============================================================
;; PHASE 1: Critical Fixes (no dependencies, parallel)
;; ============================================================

;; C1: save_handler has no ACL enforcement — privilege escalation
(given task-acl-save-handler)
(given no-deps-acl-save-handler)
(meta task-acl-save-handler
  (description "Add write ACL check to save_handler (PUT /{*path}) in routes.rs. Currently any authenticated user can overwrite any page.")
  (acceptance "save_handler calls check_page_acl_edit before writing; returns 403 for users without edit permission"))

;; C2: pending_writes never cleared on success path
(given task-pending-writes-clear)
(given no-deps-pending-writes-clear)
(meta task-pending-writes-clear
  (description "Remove path from pending_writes after successful flush write in flush.rs:70-76")
  (acceptance "pending_writes.remove called after successful fs::write; no memory leak"))

;; C3: Flush/mark_flushed race loses edits
(given task-flush-atomicity)
(given no-deps-flush-atomicity)
(meta task-flush-atomicity
  (description "Make serialize_for_flush and mark_flushed atomic — add generation counter or hold lock across both in flush.rs")
  (acceptance "Edits arriving between serialize and mark_flushed are not silently lost"))

;; C4: TTL eviction bypasses WAL, pending_writes, uses wrong path
(given task-eviction-pipeline)
(given no-deps-eviction-pipeline)
(meta task-eviction-pipeline
  (description "Fix spawn_flush_lifecycle_task eviction to use pending_writes, WAL truncation, and correct file path lookup")
  (acceptance "Eviction writes go through proper pipeline; no duplicate files; no spurious reconciliation"))

;; C5: WS ticket endpoint bypasses CSRF guard
(given task-ws-csrf)
(given no-deps-ws-csrf)
(meta task-ws-csrf
  (description "Move /api/ws/ticket behind csrf_guard middleware or add CSRF validation inside ws_ticket_handler")
  (acceptance "Cross-origin POST to /api/ws/ticket is rejected without valid CSRF token"))

;; ============================================================
;; PHASE 2: Important Fixes (no dependencies, parallel)
;; ============================================================

;; I1: Session cookie missing Secure flag
(given task-cookie-secure)
(given no-deps-cookie-secure)
(meta task-cookie-secure
  (description "Add Secure flag to session cookie when TLS is active; fix bootstrap SameSite=Lax inconsistency")
  (acceptance "Session cookie includes Secure when --tls is set; all cookies use SameSite=Strict"))

;; I2: X-Forwarded-For trusted unconditionally
(given task-ip-trust)
(given no-deps-ip-trust)
(meta task-ip-trust
  (description "Default to peer address for rate limiting; only trust proxy headers when explicitly configured")

Option A — `include_dir` crate:
  Add `include_dir = \"0.7\"` to Cargo.toml. In engine.rs:
  ```rust
  use include_dir::{include_dir, Dir};
  static BUNDLED_THEMES: Dir = include_dir!(\"$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/themes\");
  ```
  Lookup: BUNDLED_THEMES.get_file(format!(\"{theme}/{template}\"))

Option B — build.rs codegen:
  Generate a Rust source file that contains static &str constants for each theme/template pair. More control, no extra dependency.

Recommendation: Option A is simpler and well-maintained. Use it unless the dependency is unacceptable.

After this task, delete src/web/templates/ — themes/default/ is now the single source of truth for built-in templates. Update all references.

  fn bundled_template(theme: &str, name: &str) -> Option<&'static str>

1. Tier 1 (User Theme): .zetl/themes/<active-theme>/<template>.html on disk
2. Tier 2 (Bundled Theme): bundled_template(active_theme, template) from compile-time embed
3. Tier 3 (Default Fallback): bundled_template(\"default\", template) from compile-time embed

Current code only has Tier 1 (disk) and Tier 2 (hardcoded default). The change is:
- Replace the match statement in the loader with calls to bundled_template()
- Add the intermediate Tier 2 lookup for the active theme name
- Tier 3 is the final fallback to \"default\"

When --theme default: Tier 1 is skipped (existing behaviour), Tier 2 = Tier 3.
When --theme minimal: Tier 1 checks disk, Tier 2 checks bundled minimal/, Tier 3 falls back to bundled default/.
When --theme custom-user-theme: Tier 1 checks disk, Tier 2 has no bundled match (returns None), Tier 3 falls back to default.

Update validate_theme() in main.rs: currently it requires .zetl/themes/<name>/ to exist for non-default themes. It must now also accept names that match a bundled theme (bundled_theme_names().contains(theme)). A theme is valid if it exists on disk OR is bundled. Both can be true (installed shadows bundled).

;; =============================================================================
;;
;; This plan coordinates the research spikes and implementation phases defined
;; in SPEC-004. The work proceeds in two phases:
;;
;;   Phase 0: Research spikes (parallelizable) — validate critical unknowns
;;   Phase 1: Implementation — sequential phases gated on spike results
;;

;;   engineer    — implements sync subsystem
;;   architect   — reviews design decisions, resolves open questions
;;
;; Run `hence board research/plan.spl` to see full task status.
;; =============================================================================

;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; Plan Metadata
;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(meta plan
  (id "SPEC-004")
  (title "Distributed Vault Sync via Goblins Sidecar")
  (version "1.0.0")
  (status "active")
  (created "2026-02-18")
  (author "agent:architect")
  (spec "SPEC-004")
  (description "Research spikes and implementation plan for distributed vault synchronization using Spritely Goblins as a capability-secured networking sidecar. Validates Syrup-in-Rust, Goblins sidecar feasibility, and conflict detection before committing to full implementation."))

;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; Agents
;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(given agent-researcher-available)
(given agent-engineer-available)
(given agent-architect-available)

;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; Phase 0: Research Spikes (parallelizable)
;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

;; --- Spike 0a: Syrup Serialization in Rust ---
(given task-spike-syrup)
(given no-deps-spike-syrup)
(meta task-spike-syrup
  (description "Implement Syrup encode/decode in Rust. Test round-trip compatibility with Guile's Syrup implementation. Cover all types: Boolean, Integer, String, ByteString, Symbol, Record, Sequence, Set, Dictionary. Publish as standalone crate (syrup-rs). Timebox: 1 day.")
  (acceptance "100% round-trip compatibility on test vectors between Rust encoder and Guile decoder. If undocumented edge cases prevent clean round-trip, document them and recommend JSON-RPC fallback."))

;; --- Spike 0b: Goblins Sidecar Prototype ---
(given task-spike-sidecar)
(given no-deps-spike-sidecar)
(meta task-spike-sidecar
  (description "Build a minimal Goblins 0.17.0 sidecar: an actor that accepts 'list-files' and 'get-file' messages, registered on both Unix domain socket and Tor onion netlayers, with Bloblin persistence. Test local IPC from Rust and remote access from Guile. Timebox: 2 days.")
  (acceptance "Both local (Unix socket) and remote (Tor) peers can list and retrieve files from the sidecar. Actor state survives sidecar restart via Bloblin. Document any macOS compatibility issues with Tor."))

;; --- Spike 0c: Conflict Detection Accuracy ---
(given task-spike-conflicts)
(given no-deps-spike-conflicts)
(meta task-spike-conflicts
  (description "Validate that SHA-256 content hashing + mtime tracking detects all conflicts without false positives for ≤ 10K file vaults. Create two test vaults with overlapping content, simulate 100 concurrent edit scenarios. Timebox: 0.5 day.")
  (acceptance "100% true positive rate (all real conflicts detected), 0% false positive rate (identical edits not flagged). If hashing alone is insufficient, recommend line-level diffing or git integration."))

;; --- Spike 0d: Goblins macOS Installation ---
(given task-spike-install)
(given no-deps-spike-install)
(meta task-spike-install
  (description "Document and test the full Goblins 0.17.0 installation path on macOS (Homebrew). Verify: Guile 3.0+, guile-fibers, guile-gnutls, Goblins, OCapN netlayers all work. Test Unix domain socket and TCP+TLS netlayers. If Tor is problematic on macOS, document the issue and assess TCP+TLS as a sufficient alternative.")
  (acceptance "Working Goblins installation on macOS with at least Unix socket + TCP+TLS netlayers. Installation steps documented. Known issues catalogued."))

;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; Phase 0 Gate: Spike Review
;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

(given task-spike-review)
(meta task-spike-review
  (description "Review all spike results. Produce a go/no-go decision for proceeding to implementation. If any spike reveals a showstopper, propose an alternative architecture. Write findings to research/spike-review.md.")
  (acceptance "Written review covering all 4 spikes. Each spike assessed as pass/fail/conditional. Go/no-go decision with rationale. If no-go, alternative architecture proposed."))

;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
;; Phase 1: Implementation (sequential, gated on spike review)
;; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

;; --- Phase 1a: Local IPC ---
(given task-local-ipc)
(meta task-local-ipc
  (description "Implement zetl <-> sidecar communication over Unix domain socket using JSON-RPC 2.0. Add `zetl sync start/stop/status` commands. Sidecar launches as background daemon, zetl connects and sends commands. REQ-001 from SPEC-004.")
  (acceptance "`zetl sync start` launches sidecar, `zetl sync status` reports running state, `zetl sync stop` terminates gracefully. JSON-RPC round-trip works for a simple 'ping' command."))

;; --- Phase 1b: Sync Core ---
(given task-sync-core)
(meta task-sync-core
  (description "Implement the pull/push sync protocol with conflict staging. Delta-based file transfer with generation tracking. Conflict detection via SHA-256 content hash comparison. Stage conflicts in .zetl/sync/conflicts/. TCP+TLS transport (LAN only). REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006 from SPEC-004.")
  (acceptance "Pull receives new/modified files from remote. Push sends local changes. Conflicts detected and staged correctly. Sync state persisted across runs. Works over TCP+TLS on LAN."))

;; --- Phase 1c: Capabilities ---
(given task-capabilities)
(meta task-capabilities
  (description "Implement capability creation, attenuation, and revocation. `zetl sync share` generates scoped sturdyrefs. `zetl sync attenuate` creates weaker child capabilities. `zetl sync revoke` invalidates capabilities. Folder-based scope model. REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-007 from SPEC-004.")
  (acceptance "Share generates valid sturdyref with scope+permissions. Attenuated caps cannot exceed parent permissions. Revoked caps are rejected on next connection. Remote management (add/list/remove) works."))

;; --- Phase 1d: Tor Transport ---
(given task-tor-transport)
(meta task-tor-transport
  (description "Add Tor onion service as a transport option alongside TCP+TLS. Sidecar registers on both netlayers simultaneously. Sturdyrefs work across both transports. NAT traversal via Tor enables internet-wide sync without port forwarding.")
  (acceptance "Sync works between two machines on different networks via Tor. Sturdyref generated on one machine is resolvable from another. Falls back to TCP+TLS on LAN when Tor is unavailable."))

;; --- Phase 1e: Polish ---
(given task-polish)
(meta task-polish
  (description "Conflict resolution UX, --dry-run flag, audit log (.zetl/sync/log.json), improved error messages, `zetl sync conflicts` and `zetl sync resolve` commands. REQ-008 from SPEC-004.")
  (acceptance "All CON-001 through CON-007 contract specifications met. Audit log captures all operations. Dry-run shows what would change without applying. Error messages are structured JSON when -f json is specified."))
